literal: Originally stockade land; Goryeo made it Longyuan County; Bohai kept it; Liao at first abolished it.
idiomatic: Originally a stockade site; Goryeo made Longyuan County; Bohai retained it; early Liao abolished it.

literal: Shengzong on the eastern campaign restored it under the army designation.
idiomatic: Shengzong restored it on the eastern campaign, taking the army name.

literal: Originally Bohai Longhe Commandery; former counties four: Haiyang, Jiehai, Gechuan, and Longhe—all abolished.
idiomatic: Originally Bohai Longhe Commandery; four former counties—Haiyang, Jiehai, Gechuan, Longhe—all abolished.

literal: Originally Bohai Huiyi Commandery; former counties four: Huiyi, Shuiqi, Shunhua, and Meixian—all abolished.
idiomatic: Originally Bohai Huiyi Commandery; four former counties—Huiyi, Shuiqi, Shunhua, Meixian—all abolished.

literal: One hundred twenty li northeast of Kai Prefecture.
idiomatic: Kai Prefecture lay one hundred twenty li to the northeast.

literal: Originally Bohai Jili Commandery; former counties four: Honghe, Songcheng, Jili, and Shishan—all abolished.
idiomatic: Originally Bohai Jili Commandery; four former counties—Honghe, Songcheng, Jili, Shishan—all abolished.

literal: Goryeo established the prefecture; one former county called Dingdong.
idiomatic: Goryeo founded the prefecture; one former county, Dingdong.

literal: In Tonghe year 13 of Shengzong it was raised to an army; Liaoxi people were moved to fill it.
idiomatic: Shengzong Tonghe year 13 raised it to an army and settled Liaoxi households there.

literal: Subordinate to the Eastern Capital regent office.
idiomatic: Under the Eastern Capital regent office.

literal: Established by Goryeo; Liao moved Liaoxi people to dwell there.
idiomatic: Goryeo founded it; Liao relocated Liaoxi inhabitants there.

literal: Bao Prefecture, Xuanyi Army, military commissioner.
Goryeo established the prefecture; one former county called Laiyuan.
idiomatic: Goryeo founded the prefecture; one former county, Laiyuan.

literal: Because Goryeo King Xun had been installed without authorization and would not submit when questioned, at the end of Tonghe Goryeo surrendered; 7 in Kaitai year 3 Bao and Ding two prefectures were taken and a monopoly market was placed here.
idiomatic: When Goryeo King Xun was irregularly enthroned and defied inquiry, Goryeo submitted at Tonghe's end; seventh: Kaitai year 3 seized Bao and Ding and opened a monopoly market here.

literal: Subordinate to the Eastern Capital army command.
idiomatic: Under the Eastern Capital army command.

literal: Governing prefectures and armies two, counties one:
At first Liaoxi county people were moved to fill it; later seven hundred Xi and Han troops were moved to garrison.
idiomatic: Liaoxi county populations were first relocated here; later seven hundred Xi and Han soldiers garrisoned it.

literal: In Kaitai year 3 Han households were moved to establish it.
idiomatic: Kaitai year 3 settled Han households to found it.

literal: Chen Prefecture, Fengguo Army, military commissioner.
Tang Taizong with Li Shiji broke Gaimou Fort—this is that place.
idiomatic: Tang Taizong and Li Shiji stormed Gaimou Fort here.

literal: Bohai changed it to Gai Prefecture, then Chen Prefecture, named for Chenhan.
idiomatic: Bohai renamed it Gai Prefecture, then Chen Prefecture after Chenhan.

literal: Markets and lanes stood close together—it was the greatest thoroughfare.
idiomatic: Its markets and lanes crowded together—the region's chief crossroads.

literal: Liao moved its people to Zu Prefecture.
idiomatic: Liao relocated its populace to Zu Prefecture.

literal: Subordinate to the Eastern Capital regent office.
idiomatic: Under the Eastern Capital regent office.

literal: Originally Bohai Shanlu Commandery; former counties five: Shanyang, Shanlu, Hanyang, Baiyan, and Shuangyan—all abolished.
idiomatic: Originally Bohai Shanlu Commandery; five former counties—Shanyang, Shanlu, Hanyang, Baiyan, Shuangyan—all abolished.

literal: One hundred thirty li from the capital.
idiomatic: It stood one hundred thirty li from the capital.

literal: Military affairs belonged to the Southern Jurchen Tanghe Office.
idiomatic: Military affairs fell under the Southern Jurchen Tanghe Office.

literal: West to the sea fifteen li; beside the sea is Xiongyue Mountain.
idiomatic: Fifteen li west to the sea; Xiongyue Mountain stands on the coast.

literal: In Tonghe a Goryeo campaign used fierce Yan troops; two commanders were posted and a city built for defense.
idiomatic: During Tonghe's Goryeo war fierce Yan troops earned two command posts and a garrison city.

literal: Military affairs belonged to the Eastern Capital army command.
idiomatic: Military affairs under the Eastern Capital army command.

literal: Originally Han Anshi County; Goryeo made it Anshi Fort.
idiomatic: Originally Han Anshi County; Goryeo fortified it as Anshi.

literal: Tang Taizong attacked but could not take it; Xue Rengui in white robes scaled the wall—this is that place.
idiomatic: Tang Taizong failed to capture it; Xue Rengui scaled the walls in white—this was the site.

literal: Bohai established the prefecture; former counties four: Weicheng, Heduan, Cangshan, and Longzhen—8 all abolished.
idiomatic: Bohai founded the prefecture; four former counties—Weicheng, Heduan, Cangshan, Longzhen—eighth note: all abolished.

literal: Sixty li southwest of the capital.
idiomatic: Sixty li southwest of the Eastern Capital.

literal: Xing Prefecture, Zhongxing Army, military commissioner.
Bohai established the prefecture; former counties three: Shengji, Suanshan, and Tieshan—all abolished.
idiomatic: Bohai founded it; three former counties—Shengji, Suanshan, Tieshan—all abolished.

literal: Three hundred li southwest of the capital.
idiomatic: Three hundred li southwest of the capital seat.

literal: Bohai established the prefecture; 9 former counties five: Lingfeng, Changfeng, Baishi, Junyu, and Jiali—all abolished.
idiomatic: Bohai founded it; ninth note: five former counties—Lingfeng, Changfeng, Baishi, Junyu, Jiali—all abolished.

literal: One hundred li northwest of the capital.
idiomatic: One hundred li northwest of the capital seat.

literal: Bohai established the prefecture; former counties three: Chongshan, Weishui, and Lücheng—all abolished.
idiomatic: Bohai founded it; three former counties—Chongshan, Weishui, Lücheng—all abolished.

literal: One hundred fifty li northeast of the capital.
idiomatic: One hundred fifty li northeast of the Eastern Capital.

literal: Hai Prefecture, Nanhai Army, military commissioner.
Goryeo made it Shabei Fort; Tang Li Shiji once attacked it.
idiomatic: Goryeo made Shabei Fort; Tang Li Shiji once besieged it.

literal: Bohai styled it Southern Capital Nanhai Prefecture.
idiomatic: Bohai titled it Southern Capital Nanhai Prefecture.

literal: Stacked stone made the walls, nine li in circuit; it superintended Wo, Qing, and Jiao three prefectures.
idiomatic: Stacked-stone walls ran nine li; it oversaw Wo, Qing, and Jiao prefectures.

literal: Former counties six: Woju, Jiuyan, Longshan, Binhai, Shengping, and Lingquan—all abolished.
idiomatic: Six former counties—Woju, Jiuyan, Longshan, Binhai, Shengping, Lingquan—all abolished.

literal: In the Taiping era Da Yanlin rebelled; Nanhai city held firm a full year until other chieftains were captured and it surrendered.
idiomatic: In Taiping times Da Yanlin rebelled; Nanhai held a year until allied chiefs were taken and it submitted.

literal: Thereupon all people were moved to Shangjing; Qianliao County was established and Ze Prefecture people moved to fill it.
idiomatic: All inhabitants were then moved to Shangjing; Qianliao County was founded and Ze Prefecture people settled there.

literal: Governing two prefectures and one county:
